name: Tatemó
description: Michelin-starred tasting menu built around heirloom nixtamalized corn. Chef Emmanuel Chavez turned a farmers market tortilla obsession into one of the best restaurants in Texas.
must_try: $155 tasting menu — the tostadas and tamales change with the season but always hit.

name: Agnes and Sherman
description: Texas Monthly's Restaurant of the Year 2026. Asian American diner in the Heights where Chef Nick Wong does scallion-pancake waffles, French dip with Taiwanese beef broth, and a killer Rangoon dip.
must_try: French dip sandwich with Taiwanese beef broth. Or the Rangoon with wonton chips.
hours: Wed-Sun, lunch and dinner, brunch Sat-Sun

name: Le Jardinier
description: Michelin-starred French restaurant inside the Museum of Fine Arts Kinder Building. Farm-fresh, sustainably sourced. The $45 Art Lover's Lunch is a sleeper hit.
must_try: Seasonal tasting menu ($185) or Art Lover's Lunch ($45) for a steal.

name: MARCH
description: Intimate Montrose Mediterranean tasting menu from Chef Felipe Riccio and Master Sommelier June Rodil. A love letter to Mediterranean borderlands.
must_try: The tasting menu — let the kitchen and wine team take you through.

name: Da Gama
description: Portuguese-Indian fusion at M-K-T Heights. Named after Vasco da Gama. The Goan fish curry with Gulf shrimp and crab is the move.
must_try: Goan fish curry, piri piri chicken with gunpowder spice.

name: Aga's Restaurant
description: Houston Chronicle's #1 restaurant. Indo-Pak powerhouse in southwest Houston. Goat chops, biryani, and karahi that packs the house every night.
must_try: Goat chops and the lamb biryani. Go early or wait in line.

name: Killen's BBQ
description: Pearland pitmaster Ronnie Killen's temple to Texas brisket. Worth the 30-minute drive south. Arrive early — when it sells out, it's done.
must_try: Brisket. Just brisket. Maybe the beef rib on weekends.

name: Pinkerton's Barbecue
description: Heights-area BBQ with old-school Texas pits. Brisket, ribs, and a surprisingly great boudin link.
must_try: Brisket and boudin. Sides are above average for BBQ joints.

name: Feges BBQ
description: Spring Branch BBQ joint with a vegetarian-friendly twist. Korean-braised greens, elote, and a kid's play area make this a family favorite.
must_try: $15 pork steak special. The sweet and spicy sprouts are unexpectedly great.

name: Cuchara
description: 15-year Montrose institution serving Mexico City-style cuisine. Mole negro, huitlacoche quesadillas, and proper margaritas on the patio.
must_try: Turkey in mole negro. Sit on the patio when weather cooperates.

name: Zaranda
description: California-inspired Mexican from the Hugo Ortega empire. Named one of Texas Monthly's best new restaurants for 2026. Oysters with green ponzu and trout roe.
must_try: Oysters with green ponzu and trout roe.

name: Boo's Burgers
description: Walk-up burger stand on Navigation from chef Joseph Boudreaux. Cheesy smashburgers on challah buns and a mushroom sandwich that converts carnivores.
must_try: OG cheesy smashburger. The shroom sammie is the sleeper pick.

name: Camaraderie
description: Family-style fine-casual French from Chef Shawn Gawle. Manchego cheese curls, tarte flambée, and salt-baked celery root you'll photograph before eating.
must_try: Heirloom tomato pie and carrot cavatelli.

name: Yiayia's Greek Kitchen
description: Pappas Restaurants' homage to the family's Greek roots. Wood-grilled lamb chops, classic souvlaki, and a baklava cheesecake that shouldn't work but absolutely does.
must_try: Lamb chops with roasted beets and pistachio. Baklava cheesecake for dessert.

name: Handies Douzo
description: Houston's crispiest hand rolls. Three locations. Fast, fresh, and the nori crunch is real.
must_try: Spicy tuna hand roll. The salmon skin roll is underrated.

name: Aladdin Mediterranean Cuisine
description: Cafeteria-style Mediterranean in Montrose with a devoted following. Cheap, filling, and the falafel is legit.
must_try: Combo plate with falafel, hummus, and rice.

name: Latuli
description: Chef Bryan Caswell's latest. The heirloom tomato salad with tempura onion rings and Russian dressing is the dish everyone talks about.
must_try: Heirloom tomato and burrata salad with tempura onion rings.

name: Late August
description: $95 tasting menu from Chef Sergio Hidalgo. Heirloom corn tortillas, plantain-stuffed squash blossom tacos — the detail on every plate is extraordinary.
must_try: Fried squash blossom taco on nixtamalized heirloom corn tortilla.

name: Long Weekend
description: Family-friendly mega-restaurant near the Heights with Houston's largest outdoor play area, fire pits, a creek, and a full breakfast-through-dinner menu.
must_try: Breakfast tacos from the café. Let the kids loose in Creative Canyon.

name: The Breakfast Klub
description: Houston institution for wings and waffles. The line wraps around the building on weekends and nobody minds.
must_try: Wings and waffles. That's the move. Period.

name: Pappas Bros. Steakhouse
description: Classic Texas steakhouse. Big steaks, big wine list, big check. The porterhouse is worth every cent.
must_try: Bone-in ribeye or porterhouse for two.

name: Pappadeaux Seafood Kitchen
description: Gulf Coast seafood chain born in Houston. Crawfish étouffée, blackened catfish, and Cajun-spiced everything. Tourist-friendly but locals go too.
must_try: Crawfish étouffée or the fried seafood platter.

name: Hugo's
description: Chef Hugo Ortega's flagship regional Mexican in Montrose. Oaxacan mole, cochinita pibil, and a legendary Sunday brunch.
must_try: Sunday brunch buffet. The cochinita pibil is textbook.

name: Ninfa's on Navigation
description: The original home of the fajita. East End Tex-Mex legend since 1973. The tacos al carbon are non-negotiable.
must_try: Tacos al carbon — the dish that launched a thousand imitators.

name: Saint Arnold Brewing Company
description: Texas' oldest craft brewery. Massive beer garden with downtown skyline views, art cars on display, and murals by Gonzo247. The Fancy Lawnmower is Houston in a glass.
must_try: Fancy Lawnmower kölsch. Christmas Ale if you're here in winter.

name: Karbach Brewing Co.
description: Major Houston brewery with biergarten, restaurant, and Pizza & Pints. Weekend live music and festivals. Hopadillo IPA is the gateway beer.
must_try: Hopadillo IPA and the Korean Fried Chicken ($18).

name: Urban South - HTX
description: New Orleans-born brewery's Houston outpost. Known for experimental fruit sours and a chill taproom vibe.
must_try: Whatever fruit sour is on the rotating tap.

name: Eureka Heights Brew Co.
description: Heights neighborhood brewery with picnic tables, a no-frills vibe, and solid core beers. Watch parties and trivia nights.
must_try: Mini Boss Session IPA.

name: Holler Brewing Co.
description: Small-batch brewery near Washington Ave with award-winning ESB and a laid-back taproom. Dog-friendly patio.
must_try: Holler ESB — one of the best in Texas.

name: Axelrad
description: Midtown outdoor beer garden with hammocks, string lights, and rotating pizza trucks. The vibe is pure Houston — relaxed, diverse, and always a good time.
must_try: Grab a craft beer and a hammock. That's it.

name: Heights Bier Garten
description: German-inspired beer garden on North Shepherd. Big patio, big beer list, giant pretzels, and a fun family-friendly Sunday crowd.
must_try: Giant soft pretzel with beer cheese.

name: Social Beer Garden HTX
description: Houston Press Best Bar and Houston Chronicle Best Bar and Best Happy Hour 2025. Midtown beer garden with the biggest outdoor TV, rotating food trucks, and packed trivia nights.
must_try: Whatever the seasonal cocktail is. Happy hour deals are legit.

name: Augustine Lounge
description: Inside the Michelin Key hotel. The Coyote Call (mezcal, port, Blackstrap rum, raspberry) is the standout. Elevated but unfussy.
must_try: Coyote Call cocktail.

name: Starduster Lounge
description: Heights neighborhood bar with cosmic West Texas vibes in a 100-year-old building. Steak night Thursdays. Half-off cocktails at happy hour.
must_try: Pecan or Pecan? cocktail (rye, bourbon, Licor 43).

name: Johnny's Gold Brick
description: Heights cocktail bar that feels like a speakeasy but without the pretension. Strong drinks, dark lighting, good jukebox.
must_try: Old Fashioned done right.

name: White Oak Music Hall
description: Indoor/outdoor live music venue in the Heights with upstairs, downstairs, and lawn stages. National touring acts and local bands.
must_try: Check calendar for shows. The outdoor lawn shows in spring/fall are magic.

name: House of Blues Houston
description: Downtown live music institution. National touring acts, gospel brunch on Sundays, and the Bronze Peacock Room for more intimate shows.
must_try: Sunday Gospel Brunch — music, food, and soul.

name: 713 Music Hall
description: Downtown POST Houston venue. 5,000 capacity with great sightlines and sound. Major touring acts.
must_try: Check the calendar — this is Houston's best mid-size venue.

name: Jane and the Lion Bakehouse
description: Baker Jane Wild's first solo brick-and-mortar in the Heights. Pastries, breads, and baked goods from a chef with a serious following.
must_try: Whatever's fresh that morning. The croissants sell out.

name: Catalina Coffee
description: Washington Ave coffee institution. Great espresso, solid pastries, and a shaded patio that fills with laptop workers and dog walkers.
must_try: Cortado and a kolache.

name: Boomtown Coffee
description: Heights roaster-cafe with in-house roasted beans and a neighborhood vibe. Consistently one of the best cups in Houston.
must_try: Pour-over with seasonal single origin.

name: Space Center Houston
description: Official visitor center of NASA's Johnson Space Center. Touch a moon rock, tour mission control, see astronaut training facilities. Houston's #1 attraction.
must_try: Level 9 Tour for behind-the-scenes NASA access ($199.95, advance booking required).

name: Houston Museum of Natural Science
description: Five floors of exhibits, the Burke Baker Planetarium, and the Cockrell Butterfly Center. From dinosaurs to Egyptian artifacts. Free on Thursdays after 2pm.
must_try: Cockrell Butterfly Center — walk through a three-story glass rainforest full of butterflies.

name: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
description: Largest art museum in the Southwest. Nearly 70,000 works spanning antiquity to contemporary. The Kinder Building is architecturally stunning.
must_try: Visit the Kinder Building, then walk across to Le Jardinier for lunch.

name: The Menil Collection
description: World-class art collection housed in a Renzo Piano building. Surrealism, African art, antiquities — all free, always. The Rothko Chapel is across the street.
must_try: The Menil + Rothko Chapel + Cy Twombly Gallery — all free, all walkable.

name: Rothko Chapel
description: Non-denominational chapel housing 14 Mark Rothko canvases. A contemplative space unlike anything else in Texas. Barnett Newman's Broken Obelisk sculpture stands outside.
must_try: Sit in silence for 15 minutes. Just be present.

name: Houston Zoo
description: 55-acre zoo in Hermann Park with 6,000+ animals. Asian elephants, Masai giraffes, sea lions. Zoo Lights in winter is a Houston holiday tradition.
must_try: Zoo Lights (Nov-Jan) — 2 million lights, animal lanterns, hot cocoa.

name: Children's Museum Houston
description: One of the top children's museums in the US. Interactive STEM exhibits, a LEGO zone, and a water table that keeps kids busy for hours.
must_try: Free Thursday evenings 5-8pm.

name: Downtown Aquarium
description: Part aquarium, part amusement park, part restaurant. 300+ species, carnival rides, Shark Tunnel train, and stingray feeding. More fun than fancy.
must_try: Shark Tunnel train ride with the kids. Dine surrounded by fish tanks.

name: Hermann Park
description: 445-acre urban oasis. Japanese garden, miniature train, golf course, Miller Outdoor Theatre, and the gateway to the zoo and Museum District.
must_try: Ride the Hermann Park Railroad ($3.75). Walk the Japanese Garden.

name: Buffalo Bayou Park
description: 160-acre linear park along the bayou. Walking/biking trails, kayak/bike rentals, dog park, public art, and the Barbara Fish Daniel Nature Play Area for kids.
must_try: Rent a kayak or stand-up paddleboard and paddle through downtown. Sunset runs along the trail.

name: Discovery Green
description: 12-acre downtown park with free concerts, yoga, ice skating in winter, and a rotating lineup of events. The living room of downtown Houston.
must_try: Free evening concerts in spring/fall. Ice skating in winter.

name: Gerald D. Hines Waterwall Park
description: 64-foot semicircular water wall near the Galleria. Surprisingly dramatic. Instagram-famous but still worth the stop.
must_try: Stand underneath and feel the mist. Great photo op.

name: Memorial Park
description: 1,500-acre urban park with running trails, a golf course, tennis center, and mountain bike trails. The 3-mile loop is Houston's most popular run.
must_try: Morning run on the 3-mile loop, then coffee at nearby Onion Creek.

name: Sam Houston Park
description: Houston's oldest park with 9 historic buildings. Victorian wonderland with rustic bridges, streams, and walking trails. Heritage Society tours available.
must_try: Guided tour of the historic buildings ($10).

name: The Galleria
description: Texas' largest shopping center and 4th largest in the US. 400+ stores, ice skating rink, two hotels, and every luxury brand you can name.
must_try: Ice skate in the middle of a Texas summer. The irony is the fun.

name: Rice Village
description: Walkable outdoor shopping district near Rice University. Boutiques, restaurants, and a collegiate vibe. Good for an afternoon of browsing.
must_try: Browse, then grab coffee and people-watch.

name: Heights Mercantile
description: Open-air shopping center in the Heights with local boutiques, a bookstore, cycling shop, and restaurants. The vibe is curated but not stuffy.
must_try: Wander, then grab a drink at nearby Heights Bier Garten.

name: Trellis Spa
address: 5 The Houstonian, 111 N Post Oak Ln, Houston, TX 77024
description: Best spa in Houston, full stop. Outdoor water facilities, full-service treatments, and you can eat at the spa café in your robe.
must_try: Full day pass — outdoor pools, then lunch in your robe.

name: Hotel Saint Augustine
description: Michelin Key hotel. Esquire and Travel + Leisure best new hotel of 2025. Augustine Lounge bar is worth a visit even if you're not staying.
must_try: Even if you don't stay here, drink at Augustine Lounge.

name: Hotel Granduca Houston
description: Italian-style luxury boutique near the Galleria. Quiet, elegant, and Ristorante Cavour serves one of the best hotel breakfasts in the city.
must_try: Breakfast at Ristorante Cavour.

name: The Houstonian Hotel, Club & Spa
address: 111 N Post Oak Ln, Houston, TX 77024
description: 18-acre wooded resort inside the city. Home to Trellis Spa. Feels like a Hill Country retreat but you're 10 minutes from the Galleria.
must_try: Trellis Spa day + dinner at their restaurant.

name: POST Houston
description: Former post office turned mixed-use destination with 713 Music Hall, international food hall, rooftop farm, and co-working space. Houston's adaptive reuse showpiece.
must_try: Food hall for lunch, then catch a show at 713 Music Hall.

name: H-E-B
description: Texas' beloved grocery chain. Better prepared food than most restaurants. Stock your Airbnb here.
must_try: Bakery tortillas, store-brand chips and queso, Texas BBQ section.

name: Daikin Park (Minute Maid Park)
description: Home of the Houston Astros. Retractable roof, a train that chugs after home runs, and one of the best ballpark food scenes in MLB.
must_try: Catch a game. Grab Killen's BBQ inside the park.

name: NRG Stadium
description: Home of the Houston Texans and the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo. Also hosts major concerts and events.
must_try: Rodeo season (Feb-Mar) is an absolute must if you're in town.

name: Toyota Center
description: Home of the Houston Rockets and major concert venue downtown.
must_try: Rockets game or catch a major touring artist.

name: Miller Outdoor Theatre
description: Free outdoor performances March through November in Hermann Park. Shakespeare, symphony, ballet, jazz, world music — all free.
must_try: Bring a blanket and a picnic. Any show. They're all free.

name: Alley Theatre
description: Tony Award-winning regional theater in the Theater District. One of the country's leading resident theater companies.
must_try: Check the season schedule — they consistently produce excellent work.

name: Musaafer
address: 5115 Westheimer Rd Suite C-3500, Houston, TX 77056
description: Opulent, Michelin-recognized Indian dining in the Galleria with intricate multi-regional cuisine and stunning interiors.
must_try: Butter Chicken and the elaborate dessert presentations.

name: Truth BBQ
description: One of the state's elite BBQ joints. The lines wrap around the building but the immaculately rendered brisket makes the wait irrelevant.
must_try: Brisket and corn pudding.

name: Squable
description: European fare with American execution. Heights neighborhood spot with an industry-favorite happy hour and incredible baked goods.
must_try: French cheeseburger and freezer martinis.

name: Nancy's Hustle
description: EaDo powerhouse blending natural wine culture with an unabashedly rich, inventive menu that defined modern Houston dining.
must_try: Nancy Cakes with whipped butter and roe.

name: Crawfish & Noodles
description: The quintessential Houston Viet-Cajun experience. Garlic-butter drenched crawfish that perfectly encapsulate the city's fusion culture.
must_try: Viet-Cajun Crawfish — spicy, garlicky, dripping in butter.

name: Himalaya
description: Anthony Bourdain-approved institution serving incredibly bold, unapologetically spicy Indian and Pakistani fusion dishes.
must_try: Hunter's Beef Plate and Garlic Naan.

name: Little's Oyster Bar
description: Brilliantly executed modern seafood with a spectacular raw bar and elevated Gulf Coast classics.
must_try: Oysters on the half shell and caviar service.

name: Casaema
address: 5307 N Main St Suite 100, Houston, TX 77009
description: Michelin Bib Gourmand destination inspired by Mexico City. Breakfast and lunch service in the Heights that's drawn national attention.
must_try: Chilaquiles and fresh pastries.

name: Pho Binh
description: Award-winning pho institution in South Houston. The broth is the reason you drove 30 minutes and you won't regret it.
must_try: Special combo pho — the broth has been perfected over decades.

name: Credence
description: Highly refined, Texas-rooted dining in Memorial that honors local culinary traditions with precision execution.
must_try: Wood-fired steaks and seasonal seafood towers.

name: Anvil Bar & Refuge
description: The architect of Houston's craft cocktail movement. Nationally ranked, offering a flawless menu of 100 classics.
must_try: Anything from the 100 List.

name: Julep
description: James Beard Award-winning Southern cocktail bar. Refined atmosphere and perfect mint juleps.
must_try: The classic Mint Julep.

name: Lola's Depot
description: The definitive Houston dive bar. Dark, covered in stickers, aggressively cheap drinks. Play basketball out back, eat tacos from the truck next door.
must_try: Cold local beer in a koozie.

name: 8th Wonder Brewery
description: Massive EaDo institution deeply rooted in Houston sports nostalgia. Now offering THC seltzers alongside solid core beers.
must_try: Dome Foam cream ale or Wonder Water THC seltzer.

name: Bad Astronaut Brewing Co.
description: 36,000 sq ft space-themed adult playground in Northside with air hockey, lagers, and hardcore punk shows.
must_try: Fake Landing Hazy IPA.

name: West Alabama Ice House
description: Open-air Houston institution. Cheap beer, outdoor basketball court, and the most democratic patio in Montrose.
must_try: Lone Star tallboy and a taco from whatever truck is parked outside.

name: Cidercade Houston
description: Pay a flat cover for unlimited free play on hundreds of retro arcade cabinets while drinking house-made hard ciders.
must_try: Artisan thin-crust pizza while gaming.

name: Buc-ee's (Katy)
description: Nearest massive Buc-ee's to the city center. A Texas cultural phenomenon — beaver nuggets, brisket sandwiches, and pristine bathrooms.
must_try: Brisket sandwich and Beaver Nuggets.

name: Gatlin's BBQ
description: Heights-area family operation. Brisket and ribs are elite but the sides — especially the dirty rice — are what keep people coming back.
must_try: Brisket and dirty rice.

name: Goode Company BBQ
description: Houston institution since 1977. Czech-style sausage and mesquite-smoked brisket in a barn-like setting. Tourist-friendly but locals still go.
must_try: Czech sausage and jalapeño pinto beans.

name: Blood Bros. BBQ
description: Asian-Texan BBQ fusion in Bellaire. Vietnamese-Cajun boudin, smoked turkey banh mi, and brisket fried rice push boundaries while honoring both traditions.
must_try: Brisket fried rice and smoked turkey banh mi.

name: The Pit Room
description: Montrose BBQ joint with a massive covered patio. Pulled pork and beef ribs are the stars. Great happy hour too.
must_try: Beef ribs (weekends only) and pulled pork sandwich.

name: El Tiempo Cantina
description: Laurenzo family Tex-Mex dynasty. Multiple locations but Navigation is the original. Sizzling fajitas arrive and the whole restaurant smells incredible.
must_try: Beef fajitas — the sizzle is half the experience.

name: Teotihuacan Mexican Cafe
description: No-frills Heights-area Mexican with massive portions and breakfast plates that feed two. The green salsa is liquid gold.
must_try: Chilaquiles or huevos rancheros. Green salsa on everything.

name: Coltivare
description: Garden-to-table Italian in the Heights with a working garden you can see from the patio. Wood-fired pizzas and handmade pasta.
must_try: Any seasonal wood-fired pizza. The garden salad is legitimately incredible.

name: Sylvia's Enchilada Kitchen
description: Sylvia Casares is the Enchilada Queen of Texas. Regional Mexican enchiladas from every corner of Mexico. This is the real thing.
must_try: Enchilada sampler — try all the regional styles.

name: Uchi Houston
description: Austin import that's become a Montrose staple. Japanese farmhouse-inspired with creative omakase and incredible hot/cold tastings.
must_try: Maguro & Goat Cheese or any omakase option.

name: Kata Robata
description: Four-time James Beard nominee Chef Hori's sushi temple. Fish flown from Japan multiple times weekly. The omakase is unforgettable.
must_try: Omakase tasting or the $28 chirashi bowl at lunch.

name: Pepper Twins
description: Fiery Sichuan in River Oaks. The spice levels are real. Cumin lamb and mapo tofu that'll make you sweat and order more.
must_try: Cumin lamb and dry-fried chicken.

name: Mala Sichuan Bistro
description: Asiatown Sichuan heavyweight. The dan dan noodles and boiled fish in chili oil are the gold standard in Houston.
must_try: Dan dan noodles and boiled fish in chili oil.

name: Tiger Den
description: Houston's best ramen. Rich tonkotsu broth and thick noodles in a no-frills setting. Worth the drive to Bellaire.
must_try: Tonkotsu ramen with extra chashu.

name: Huynh Restaurant
description: EaDo Vietnamese hole-in-the-wall. Vermicelli bowls and banh mi that locals have been eating for decades. Cash only.
must_try: Vermicelli bowl with grilled pork.

name: Moon Rabbit
description: Modern Vietnamese in the Heights. CultureMap Tastemaker nominee bringing elevated takes on classics.
must_try: Shaking beef and pho specials.

name: North China
description: Heights institution for hand-pulled noodles and Mandarin-style cooking since 1976. Unpretentious, excellent, cash-friendly.
must_try: Hand-pulled noodles and Peking pork chops.

name: State of Grace
description: Modern Gulf Coast Southern in a gorgeous River Oaks-adjacent space. Raw bar, wood-grilled meats, and an excellent cocktail program.
must_try: Oyster platter and wood-grilled whole fish.

name: Goode Company Seafood
description: Houston classic for Gulf Coast seafood. Campechana, fried catfish, and a mesquite-grilled redfish that's been on the menu for decades.
must_try: Mesquite-grilled redfish and campechana.

name: Lucille's
description: Museum District Southern fine dining from chef Chris Williams. Gulf Coast soul food elevated with technique and gorgeous plating.
must_try: Oxtail and Gulf shrimp. Sunday brunch is special.

name: Theodore Rex
description: Chef Justin Yu's downtown restaurant serving Texas-rooted seasonal tasting menus. One of Houston's most respected kitchens.
must_try: The seasonal tasting menu — trust the kitchen.

name: B&B Butchers & Restaurant
description: Washington Ave steakhouse with an in-house butcher shop. Dry-aged prime cuts and a killer rooftop bar for pre-dinner drinks.
must_try: 44oz Tomahawk Ribeye. Rooftop bar first.

name: Vic & Anthony's
description: Downtown power steakhouse. Dark wood, white tablecloths, and steaks that compete with anyone in Texas.
must_try: Porterhouse for two and the lobster bisque.

name: Steak 48
description: River Oaks steakhouse with a scene. Great food, great drinks, and you'll see Houston's dressed-up crowd on weekends.
must_try: Bone-in filet and the tableside Caesar.

name: Dolce Vita
description: Montrose Italian with a massive patio and late-night energy. Neapolitan-style pizza and housemade pasta in a lively, see-and-be-seen setting.
must_try: Margherita pizza and any fresh pasta.

name: Tony's
description: Houston's most legendary fine dining room since 1965. Italian-Continental cuisine in a River Oaks setting that defines old-school Houston luxury.
must_try: Dover sole and the veal chop.

name: Oporto Fooding House
description: Portuguese cuisine in Greenway Plaza from the team behind Da Gama. Excellent seafood, natural wines, and a beautiful bar program.
must_try: Portuguese-style grilled octopus and piri piri prawns.

name: Bravery Chef Hall
description: Downtown chef-driven food hall with rotating micro-restaurants. Higher-end than a typical food court — these are real chefs.
must_try: Check what's rotating — concepts change.

name: Common Bond Bistro & Bakery
description: Montrose bakery-café with croissants rivaling Paris and a brunch menu that draws long weekend lines.
must_try: Twice-baked almond croissant and shakshuka.

name: Baby Barnaby's
description: Montrose breakfast institution. Quirky, colorful, and the migas are the reason you're here.
must_try: Migas and any pancake special.

name: Kau Ba
description: Midtown Vietnamese with a cocktail bar attached. Elevated pho, banh xeo, and a killer happy hour.
must_try: Banh xeo (crispy Vietnamese crepe).

name: Nonno's Family Pizza Tavern
description: Heights neighborhood pizza joint that's become a CultureMap Tastemaker nominee. Family-friendly, great pies, solid beer list.
must_try: Any specialty pizza. The garlic knots are dangerous.

name: Chardon
address: Thompson Houston, 811 Main St, Houston, TX 77002
description: Thompson Hotel restaurant from veteran Houston chef E.J. Miller. Texas-spin on French classics — wagyu beef cheek bourguignon, foie gras with cornbread.
must_try: Texas wagyu beef cheek bourguignon.

name: Perseid
description: Hotel restaurant that earned a Bon Appetit best new restaurant nod. Genre-bending dishes like crawfish sausage.
must_try: Crawfish sausage and seasonal tasting menu.

name: Frost Town Brewing
description: EaDo brewery in a beautiful brick building. German-inspired lagers and excellent food. Nice outdoor seating.
must_try: German-style pilsner and the burger.

name: Buffalo Bayou Brewing Co.
description: Massive brewery near Washington Ave with a gorgeous taproom. Known for 1836 Copper Ale and creative seasonals.
must_try: 1836 Copper Ale.

name: Poison Girl
description: Montrose dive bar institution. Cheap drinks, a killer jukebox, and a whiskey wall that commands respect.
must_try: Whiskey and whatever's cheapest on draft.

name: Better Luck Tomorrow
description: Heights cocktail bar from Bobby Heugel (Anvil). Casual neighborhood joint with serious drinks and great bar food.
must_try: The burger is legendary. Any cocktail is good.

name: Lei Low Bar
description: Heights tiki bar with a perfect backyard vibe. Rum-forward cocktails and string lights in the trees. Date night gold.
must_try: Any tiki cocktail — they're all legit.

name: Goodnight Charlie's
description: Montrose honky tonk. Two-stepping, live country bands, and whiskey shots. It's more fun than you expect it to be.
must_try: Get on the dance floor for two-step night.

name: Continental Club Houston
description: Austin transplant in Midtown. Intimate live music venue with rockabilly, blues, soul, and country acts. No bad seats.
must_try: Check the calendar — shows almost every night.

name: Warehouse Live
description: EaDo music venue with two stages. Touring indie, hip-hop, and electronic acts. The Ballroom stage is intimate perfection.
must_try: See a show in the Ballroom — smaller stage, better sound.

name: Last Concert Cafe
description: Outdoor music venue near downtown with a hippie soul. Tex-Mex food, cold beer, and live bands under the trees.
must_try: Enchiladas and a Shiner while the band plays.

name: Rudyard's British Pub
description: Montrose institution with live music upstairs and a proper pub downstairs. Trivia nights are fierce. One of Houston's best burgers.
must_try: Rudyard's burger and trivia night.

name: Grand Prize Bar
description: Montrose neighborhood bar with strong cocktails at dive bar prices. The patio is great and the jukebox is curated.
must_try: Old Fashioned — surprisingly excellent for a dive.

name: Numbers Night Club
description: Legendary Montrose goth/industrial/new wave club since 1978. Three rooms of music, cheap drinks, and Houston's most unique crowd.
must_try: Friday or Saturday night for the full experience.

name: Moon Tower Inn
description: EaDo hot dog and craft beer spot with a massive outdoor area. Gourmet sausages, local beers, and neighborhood vibes.
must_try: Wild game sausage and a local draft.

name: Blacksmith
description: Montrose third-wave coffee in a gorgeous converted blacksmith shop. Same team as Anvil Bar. Serious espresso.
must_try: Cortado and any pastry.

name: Common Bond
description: Best bakery in Houston. The twice-baked almond croissant is legendary. Multiple locations but Montrose is the original.
must_try: Twice-baked almond croissant.

name: Fluff Bake Bar
description: Rebecca Masson's dessert bar in Midtown. Bourbon caramel brownies and seasonal pies that justify the trip alone.
must_try: Bourbon caramel brownies and any seasonal pie.

name: Fat Cat Creamery
description: Heights ice cream shop with small-batch, locally sourced flavors. Mexican Hot Chocolate and seasonal rotations.
must_try: Mexican Hot Chocolate or Lemon Buttermilk Pie.

name: Shipley Do-Nuts
description: Houston institution since 1936. The glazed donut is the benchmark. Kolaches are the real reason to go.
must_try: Glazed donut and a sausage/cheese kolache.

name: Contemporary Arts Museum Houston
description: Always free contemporary art museum. Rotating exhibitions of cutting-edge work. Perfect pairing with MFAH across the street.
must_try: Whatever the current exhibition is — it changes frequently.

name: Holocaust Museum Houston
description: Nation's fourth-largest Holocaust museum. Three-story campus with WWII railcar, 50+ interactive screens, and deeply moving survivor testimonies.
must_try: The permanent Holocaust gallery with the German railcar.

name: Asia Society Texas Center
description: Stunning Yoshio Taniguchi-designed building. Asian art, cultural programming, and film screenings. Free general admission.
must_try: Architecture alone is worth the visit. Check for film screenings.

name: The Health Museum
description: Interactive science and health museum in the Museum District. Great for kids — walk through a giant human body.
must_try: Amazing Body Gallery — walk-through human body.

name: Houston Center for Photography
description: Free photography gallery and community space in Montrose. Rotating exhibitions and a strong library collection.
must_try: Current exhibition — always free.

name: Buffalo Soldiers National Museum
description: Only US museum dedicated to the African-American soldier. Currently closed for major renovation — check before visiting.
must_try: Call ahead — closed through Summer 2026 for renovations.

name: Beer Can House
description: House covered in 50,000 flattened beer cans. Pure Houston weirdness. Quick stop but completely unforgettable.
must_try: Just stand there and absorb the insanity.

name: Art Car Museum
description: Tiny Heights museum celebrating Houston's art car culture. Free, weird, and wonderfully Houston.
must_try: See the cars, then watch the Art Car Parade in April.

name: MATCH - Midtown Arts & Theater Center
description: Midtown performing arts complex with multiple theater spaces. Local dance, theater, film, and comedy productions.
must_try: Check the calendar — diverse programming from Houston's independent arts scene.

name: Bayou Bend Collection & Gardens
description: MFAH property in River Oaks. 14 acres of gardens and a mansion filled with American decorative arts. Feels like stepping into a different era.
must_try: Spring garden tour when the azaleas bloom.

name: Market Square Park
description: Houston's oldest public square, beautifully restored. Dog park, public art, and surrounded by downtown restaurants and bars.
must_try: Grab coffee and people-watch. Dog park if you brought yours.

name: Brazos Bend State Park
description: 45 miles south of Houston. Alligators, birdwatching, and the George Observatory for stargazing. The most Texas nature experience near the city.
must_try: Hike the Elm Lake trail for guaranteed alligator sightings. George Observatory on Saturday nights.

name: Waugh Drive Bat Colony
description: 250,000 Mexican free-tailed bats emerge at sunset from under the Waugh Drive bridge. Free, weird, and very Houston.
must_try: Arrive 30 min before sunset. Stand on the east side of the bridge.

name: Eleanor Tinsley Park
description: Downtown park along Buffalo Bayou with the best skyline photo spot in Houston. Site of major festivals and July 4th fireworks.
must_try: Skyline photos at golden hour.

name: BCycle Houston
description: Bike share system with stations across inner Houston. Great for Buffalo Bayou trails or getting between Museum District spots.
must_try: Day pass + ride the Buffalo Bayou trail from downtown to Shepherd Dr.

name: M-K-T Heights
description: Mixed-use development in the Heights with restaurants (Da Gama), shops, fitness, and a food hall. The Heights' answer to a lifestyle center.
must_try: Dinner at Da Gama then browse the shops.

name: River Oaks District
description: Open-air luxury shopping district. Hermès, Cartier, Dior alongside upscale restaurants. Houston's most aspirational retail experience.
must_try: Window shop if nothing else. Steak 48 is right here.

name: Houston Farmers Market
description: Year-round farmers market near the Heights. Local produce, prepared foods, and a great Saturday morning outing.
must_try: Saturday morning for the best selection. Grab breakfast tacos.

name: Hiatus Spa + Retreat
description: Greenway-area day spa with a strong cocktail of treatments. Popular for couples packages and relaxation.
must_try: Couples massage package.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Houston
description: Downtown luxury overlooking Discovery Green. Bayou & Bottle bar, excellent pool, and walkable to Theater District.
must_try: Drinks at Bayou & Bottle bar. Pool on a hot day.

name: Hotel ZaZa Museum District
description: Boutique luxury in the Museum District. Themed concept suites, rooftop pool, and Z on 23 bar. Walking distance to museums.
must_try: Concept suites if you're splurging. Z on 23 rooftop bar.

name: La Colombe d'Or Hotel
description: Boutique art hotel in Montrose. 32 rooms starting at $500/night. Original art collection throughout, upscale restaurant and cocktail bar.
must_try: The art collection and the restaurant.

name: Thompson Houston
description: Downtown luxury with Chardon restaurant and a scene-y rooftop pool. Modern design, walkable to everything downtown.
must_try: Dinner at Chardon, drinks at the rooftop.

name: Marriott Marquis Houston
description: Downtown convention hotel famous for its Texas-shaped lazy river pool on the rooftop. Instagram-famous for a reason.
must_try: Float the Texas-shaped lazy river. Seriously.

name: The Lancaster Hotel
description: Historic boutique in the Theater District. Built 1926. Walking distance to Alley Theatre, Jones Hall, and Wortham Center.
must_try: Pre-show dinner at the restaurant, walk to theater.

name: Shell Energy Stadium
description: Home of the Houston Dynamo (MLS) and Houston Dash (NWSL). EaDo location means brewery crawls before and after matches.
must_try: Hit 8th Wonder Brewery before the match.

name: The Secret Group
description: EaDo comedy club and bar with stand-up, improv, and variety shows. Houston's best comedy venue. Cheap drinks.
must_try: Any stand-up night. Check calendar for touring headliners.

name: TopGolf Webster
description: Driving range meets sports bar. Three floors of hitting bays, food, drinks. Good for groups who want to do something active.
must_try: Rent a bay, order nachos, hit golf balls. Simple.

name: Georgia James
description: Chris Shepherd's whole-animal steakhouse. Wood-fired prime cuts, heritage breeds, and one of the best cocktail programs attached to a restaurant.
must_try: 44oz Tomahawk and the smoked beef cheek.

name: Underbelly Hospitality
description: Chris Shepherd's flagship empire. The original Underbelly closed but the hospitality group (Georgia James, Wild Oats, etc.) defines modern Houston dining.
must_try: Visit any Shepherd property — they're all excellent.

name: El Tiempo Cantina (Montrose)
description: Laurenzo family Tex-Mex empire — this Montrose location is the most visitor-friendly. Sizzling fajita platters and strong margaritas.
must_try: Beef fajitas and a top-shelf margarita.

name: Annam
description: Elegant Vietnamese near Autry Park. Flavor-packed fish heads, lobster asparagus soup, and European-inspired interiors.
must_try: Lobster asparagus soup and shaking filet mignon.

name: Maximo
description: Chef Adrian Torres brought new energy with a milanesa & spaghetti verde that marries Italian technique with Mexican soul.
must_try: Milanesa & Spaghetti Verde.

name: Roegels Barbecue Co.
description: West Houston BBQ sleeper. Brisket and ribs that compete with the bigger names without the tourist lines.
must_try: Brisket and loaded baked potato.

name: 100% Taquito
description: Tiny taqueria chain with authentic street-style tacos. The al pastor is the real deal — spit-roasted and sliced to order.
must_try: Al pastor tacos. That's it. That's the order.

name: Superica
description: Heights Tex-Mex from Ford Fry. Wood-grilled fajitas, queso flameado, and a patio that's always packed.
must_try: Wood-grilled fajitas and queso flameado.

name: BCN Taste & Tradition
description: Spanish fine dining in Montrose. Paella, Ibérico ham, and a wine list that takes Barcelona seriously.
must_try: Paella Valenciana and Ibérico ham.

name: Hay Merchant
description: Montrose gastropub with 80 taps and a burger that's in the Houston hall of fame. Chris Shepherd adjacent.
must_try: The burger and whatever's interesting on the 80-tap draft wall.

name: Toasted Yolk Café
description: Houston-born brunch chain. Solid eggs Benedict variations, churro donuts, and build-your-own mimosa flights.
must_try: Churro donuts and a mimosa flight.

name: Don Café
description: Asiatown institution for Vietnamese iced coffee and banh mi. Cash-friendly, no-frills, and the drip coffee is thick and sweet.
must_try: Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá) and a banh mi.

name: Banana Leaf
description: Malaysian restaurant on Bellaire Blvd. Roti canai, laksa, and nasi lemak in a strip mall that's easy to miss and impossible to forget.
must_try: Roti canai and laksa.

name: Jinya Ramen Bar
description: Midtown ramen chain with consistently good tonkotsu. Not the most authentic, but reliable and well-located.
must_try: Tonkotsu Black ramen.

name: Silk Road
address: Courtyard by Marriott, West U area, Houston, TX
description: Unlikely dim sum success story inside a hotel. Crispy shrimp cheung fun with chili oil that rivals any Chinatown spot.
must_try: Crispy Shrimp Cheung Fun.

name: Fielding's Steak
description: Woodlands steakhouse from the Fielding's team. Worth the 30-min drive north for serious dry-aged beef and cocktails.
must_try: Dry-aged ribeye.

name: Platypus Brewing
description: Cozy Rice Village brewery with rotating experimental beers. Small space, big flavors, neighborhood vibe.
must_try: Whatever seasonal is on — they rotate constantly.

name: SpindleTap Brewery
description: North Houston brewery known for hazy IPAs and a massive taproom. Houston Haze is the flagship.
must_try: Houston Haze IPA.

name: Great Heights Brewing
description: Heights brewery with solid German-inspired lagers and a breakfast pastry counter. Unique pairing of baked goods and beer.
must_try: Pair a pastry with a pilsner — it works.

name: Walking Stick Brewing Co.
address: 1902 Washington Ave Suite E, Houston, TX 77007
description: Washington Ave brewery with a cool industrial vibe. Solid IPA lineup and rotating seasonals.
must_try: Citrus Gose.

name: Reserve 101
description: Downtown whiskey bar with 300+ bottles. Leather chairs, dark wood, and bartenders who know their stuff.
must_try: Ask the bartender for a whiskey flight based on your preferences.

name: The Toasted Coconut
description: Heights tropical bar from Bobby Heugel and Justin Yu. Rum drinks, seafood menu, and a breezy patio.
must_try: Piña colada and fried fish tacos.

name: Little Woodrow's (Midtown)
description: Texas chain sports bar with a massive outdoor area. Cheap beer, cornhole, and every game on TV. Multiple Houston locations.
must_try: Bucket of Lone Stars and a game on the big screen.

name: Scout Bar
description: Clear Lake-area live music venue near Space Center Houston. Touring rock and country acts in an intimate setting.
must_try: Pair with a Space Center visit — it's nearby.

name: Siphon Coffee
description: Montrose micro-roaster with precise pour-overs and a tiny, focused space. For the coffee nerd who wants craft over ambiance.
must_try: Single-origin pour-over.

name: Paper Co. Café
description: Washington Ave café in a converted warehouse. Good coffee, pastries, and enough space to actually sit and work.
must_try: Latte and a kolache.

name: Kolache Shoppe
description: Elevated kolaches with creative fillings — brisket, Thai chicken, spinach feta. The Czech-Texas staple, upgraded.
must_try: Brisket kolache and Thai chicken kolache.

name: Three Brothers Bakery
description: Holocaust survivor-founded bakery since 1949. Pecan pie that wins national awards. A Houston institution with deep history.
must_try: Pecan pie — award-winning.

name: Hobby Center for the Performing Arts
description: Theater District anchor for touring Broadway shows. The Houston stop on national tours. Beautiful lobby and great sightlines.
must_try: Catch whatever Broadway touring show is in town.

name: Wortham Theater Center
description: Home of Houston Ballet and Houston Grand Opera. Twin-theater complex in the Theater District.
must_try: Houston Ballet performance — world-class company.

name: Jones Hall for the Performing Arts
description: Home of the Houston Symphony. Classical, pops, and special event concerts in a grand downtown hall.
must_try: Houston Symphony performance — check for pops or classical.

name: National Museum of Funeral History
description: Exactly what it sounds like. Presidential funeral exhibits, antique hearses, and the history of embalming. Weird Houston at its finest.
must_try: The presidential funeral exhibit and fantasy coffins from Ghana.

name: Uptown Park
description: Open-air luxury lifestyle center near the Galleria. European-feeling courtyard with boutiques and upscale restaurants.
must_try: Browse and lunch at Hotel Granduca's restaurant next door.

name: Highland Village
description: Open-air center in River Oaks area. Williams Sonoma, Anthropologie, and boutiques in a walkable setting.
must_try: Browse, then walk to nearby restaurants on Westheimer.

name: Buffalo Exchange (Montrose)
description: Montrose vintage and secondhand clothing. Well-curated racks at thrift prices. Good for unique Houston finds.
must_try: Vintage denim section.

name: Milk + Honey Spa
description: Rice Village day spa with a calm, modern vibe. Excellent facials and massages. Popular for couples.
must_try: Couples massage or a facial.

name: Black Swan Yoga
description: Donation-based heated yoga in Montrose and Heights. Sweaty, intense, and accessible to all levels and budgets.
must_try: Any heated vinyasa class — pay what you can.

name: H-E-B Buffalo Speedway
description: Closest H-E-B to Museum District. Stock your Airbnb here — the prepared food section is better than most restaurants.
must_try: Sushi bar, bakery tortillas, Texas BBQ section.

name: H-E-B Heights
description: Heights H-E-B near 19th Street. Good selection, prepared foods, and right in the middle of the walkable Heights corridor.
must_try: Bakery and the deli counter.

name: CVS Pharmacy (Downtown)
description: Downtown pharmacy for tourist essentials — sunscreen, OTC meds, snacks. Walking distance from most downtown hotels.

name: Rover Oaks Pet Resort
description: Montrose pet boarding and daycare. Convenient inner-loop location if you're traveling with a dog and need coverage for a museum day.
must_try: Day boarding so you can hit attractions without guilt.

name: Enterprise Rent-A-Car (IAH Airport)
address: George Bush Intercontinental Airport, Houston, TX 77032
description: Major rental car option at IAH. All major agencies on-site via rental car shuttle. Book ahead — Houston requires a car.

name: METRO Light Rail
description: Red Line connects Downtown-Midtown-Museum District-Medical Center-NRG Park. Green/Purple lines serve EaDo and Southeast. $1.25 per ride, $3 day pass.
must_try: Red Line from Downtown to Museum District — most useful tourist route.

name: TDECU Stadium
description: Home of the University of Houston Cougars football. Big 12 conference games in a modern stadium near campus.
must_try: UH game day atmosphere — the Coog fan base is passionate.

name: Game Show Studio Houston
description: Interactive game show experience where you're the contestant. Teams compete in trivia, physical challenges, and party games. Great for groups.
must_try: Book a private group show for max fun.

name: iFLY Indoor Skydiving
description: Indoor skydiving in a vertical wind tunnel. 2-flight packages start around $70. Fun for families and thrill-seekers.
must_try: First-timer 2-flight package.
